children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child or children:

**How old is each child you're claiming for?** 

Please tell me the names and ages of all the children you'd like me to assess. This will help me determine which rules apply to them:

- **Children under 16** automatically qualify (as long as other general eligibility requirements are met)
- **Children aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **Children aged 20 or over** don't qualify for Child Benefit

What are the ages of your children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he automatically qualifies on the age requirement. However, there are still some other eligibility checks we need to go through to confirm your overall eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me move forward with the next checks:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Now I need to check a few more things about Alex's circumstances:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is typically not an issue for children his age, but I need to confirm for completeness. Please let me know - is Alex in any kind of paid employment?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8, so he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's perfectly fine - Alex is in primary school and not working, so that requirement is met.

Let me continue with the next eligibility check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now, another standard check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

This is very unlikely at his age, but I need to confirm. Is Alex receiving either of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's just 8.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Another quick check:

**Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?**

Since he's only 8 and in primary school, the answer is almost certainly no, but I need to confirm for completeness.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's only 8 and in primary school, so he's nowhere near apprenticeship age.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense. Now let me move on to check your eligibility as the claimant:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency situation. There are several paths that could make you eligible here. Let me ask you some questions to determine which applies to you:

**First, do you normally live in the UK?**

This is the most straightforward path - if you live in the UK as your main place of residence, you would meet this requirement. Please let me know:

1. Do you normally live in the UK? OR
2. If you don't, do you have any of these special circumstances:
   - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
   - Pre-settled status and working/job-seeking/studying/have sufficient resources/are a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
   - Working abroad as a Crown servant in certain qualifying countries

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live in Leeds.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK in Leeds, so you meet the residency requirement.

Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. This can be met in a few ways:

**Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **Do you live with Alex?** (This is the main way responsibility is established)

OR

2. **Do you contribute to Alex's upkeep** even if you don't live with him? This could include paying for things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or gifts - at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount.

OR

3. **Are you paying maintenance** towards Alex under a court order or formal agreement?

What's your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum. And I'm not currently contributing financially towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask a follow-up question to make sure I have the full picture:

**Are you paying any maintenance towards Alex under a court order or any formal agreement with his mum?**

This could be:
- Child support ordered by a court
- A maintenance agreement you've made with his mother
- Any formal arrangement for payments towards his care

If you're not paying anything at all towards Alex's upkeep through any of these means, then unfortunately you wouldn't meet the responsibility requirement for Child Benefit, as you need to either:
- Live with the child, OR
- Contribute financially to their upkeep (including through maintenance payments)

What's your situation regarding maintenance or support payments?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not paying any maintenance - there's no court order or formal agreement in place, and I'm not contributing anything financially at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Unfortunately, based on the information you've provided, I need to give you the outcome of this assessment.

Since you don't live with Alex and you're not contributing financially to his upkeep (either through informal contributions or formal maintenance payments), you don't meet the responsibility requirement for Child Benefit.

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you must be responsible for the child, which means either:
- **Living with the child**, OR
- **Contributing to their upkeep** (at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount, which could be through food, clothes, housing, gifts, or other care contributions), OR
- **Paying maintenance** under a court order or formal agreement

**However, I should note:** It's possible that **Alex's mother** (his custodial parent) could be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, as she lives with him and is responsible for his upkeep.

If you're interested in supporting Alex's care in the future, you could:
1. Make a formal maintenance arrangement or court order, which would then establish your responsibility
2. Begin contributing financially to his upkeep
3. Seek to have him live with you (or part-time)

For more information about Child Benefit and your options, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. So just to be clear - because Alex doesn't live with me and I'm not paying towards his upkeep, I'm not eligible for Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's correct. Based on the eligibility rules, you are **not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** because you don't meet the responsibility requirement.

To summarize your situation:
- ✅ Alex is 8 years old (qualifies on age)
- ✅ Alex is not working full-time
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (Leeds) - meets residency requirement
- ❌ **You are not responsible for Alex** - You don't live with him AND you're not contributing financially to his upkeep

The responsibility requirement is crucial for Child Benefit eligibility. Since neither of these conditions are met, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

However, as I mentioned, **Alex's mother** (who he lives with and who is responsible for his care) would likely be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, assuming she meets the other eligibility requirements like residency in the UK.

If you'd like to discuss your options going forward or have other questions about Child Benefit, feel free to ask. You can also visit https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility for more information.
